text: Ran the whole 10k without walking. Me. The person who used to hide from PE. I did that with my own legs.
Ran the 10k with Tasha this morning and we laughed the whole way round. Sunshine, bad jokes, bacon rolls after. Great day.
Signed up for the 10k in June! Never done one. Already picked the playlist. Can't wait to see what I can do.
Finished the bookshelf. Cut every piece myself, no kit, and it's square. I didn't think I had that in me.
New bookshelf's up and all the books are finally out of their boxes. The room feels like mine now. Smiling at it from the sofa.
Timber arrives Saturday for the bookshelf. I've drawn the plan four times. Itching to get the saw out.
Got through the whole presentation without reading my notes once. Six months ago I couldn't speak in a meeting. I earned that.
Presentation done and the whole team went for lunch after. Lovely afternoon, nobody talked about work. Feeling light.
Presenting to the whole company next Friday. First time. Nervous energy fizzing all day, in a good way. Bring it on.
Mira read her first whole book to me tonight. Every word. She worked so hard for that and I watched her do it.
Mira and I read in the big chair all evening with the rain going. Her head on my arm. One of those evenings.
Mira's first school trip is tomorrow and she's packed her bag three times. Honestly I'm as giddy as she is.
Paid off the credit card. Every penny, two years of saying no to things. Nobody helped. I did it.
Credit card cleared and I treated myself to the good coffee and a walk by the river. Felt like a holiday.
Last payment on the card goes out Friday. Then the savings start. I keep doing the sums for fun.
Sold my first painting today. A stranger paid actual money for something I made. Standing a bit taller tonight.
Spent all Sunday painting with the radio on and the door open. Didn't finish anything. Didn't need to. Happy as anything.
The gallery wants to see my portfolio on Thursday! I've been pacing the flat since the email came.
Told Dad the truth about the job tonight, calmly, without backing down. I've never managed that before. I'm still shaking a bit but I did it.
Dad came for dinner and told the story about the goat again and we all cried laughing. Good to have him here.
Dad lands on Saturday for two whole weeks. First time in three years. Already planning every day.
Kept my temper through the whole meeting with Hugo. Didn't rise to one thing. That took everything I had and I managed it.
Lunch with Hugo turned into three hours of nonsense and I've not laughed like that in months.
Hugo's got us tickets for the final. The actual final. I keep checking they're real.
The garden I dug from a patch of rubble has its first tomatoes. Two years of my own hands. Look at it.
Ate the first tomatoes straight off the plant, warm, with salt. The whole afternoon smelled of summer.
Seeds ordered for the garden: six kinds of tomato and something purple I've never heard of. Spring can't come fast enough.
Passed the driving test. Third go, forty-one years old, every mirror checked. I kept at it when I wanted to quit.
First drive on my own, windows down, music up, nowhere in particular. Grinning at the roundabouts.
Driving test is at nine tomorrow. I know the route. I know the car. Stomach fizzing. Let's go.
Wrote the hard email to the landlord and sent it. Polite, firm, every date listed. I stood up for myself for once.
Landlord's finally fixed the heating and the flat is warm for the first time since October. Toes out of socks. Bliss.
Keys to the new flat on Monday. Our own place, no landlord. I've already bought the doormat.
Stayed off the cigarettes for ninety days. Through the breakup, through the funeral. I didn't think I was this strong.
Ninety days smoke-free and my sense of smell is back. Walked past the bakery this morning and nearly cried with how good it was.
Booked the trip I promised myself if I made it to ninety days. Three weeks away. I keep opening the confirmation.
Stood up at Nan's funeral and gave the eulogy without my voice breaking. She'd have said well done, love. I did her justice.
Found a tape of Nan singing in the loft. Played it three times. The kitchen was full of her for an hour.
Nan's ninetieth is on Sunday and the whole family's coming. Forty of us. I can't stop planning the cake.
Made partner. Twelve years, two babies, one divorce, and nobody handed me a thing. I built this.
Team took me out to celebrate the partnership and Ayo made a speech that had me in bits. Lovely, lovely night.
They announce the new partners on Thursday. I think it's me. I can't sit still. Three more sleeps.
Went to the gym alone for the first time and didn't leave after ten minutes. Did the whole plan. Small, but it's mine.
Gym was empty and I had the whole place to myself with my own music. Bounced home. Great start to a Saturday.
New gym opens Monday, two minutes from the flat, with a pool! Already laid out my kit like a child before a trip.
Theo got the apprenticeship. He did every application himself, I just drove. My boy. My quiet, stubborn boy.
Theo came home for the weekend and we did nothing but eat and watch bad telly. The house is loud again. I love it.
Theo starts the apprenticeship on Monday. New boots by the door, alarm set. He's buzzing and so am I.
Fixed the washing machine myself with a video and a screwdriver. Saved two hundred quid and felt like a wizard.
Clean sheets, sun on the line, the smell of them when they came in. Simple, perfect day.
New washing machine comes tomorrow, the one that actually spins. I'm absurdly thrilled about an appliance.
The team hit the target I set in January, the one everyone said was mad. I set it. I got us there.
Target hit and the boss let us all go home at two. Walked in the park in the sun with nothing to do. Grand.
Bonus lands next week and I've already got the tab open for the trip. Rome in May. Me. Finally.
Said no to the extra shift. Said it clearly and didn't apologise. First time in six years. Backbone, at last.
Day off and the sun came out and I sat in the garden with a book and a cold drink and the cat. Nothing better.
Two weeks off starting Friday. Two whole weeks. Counting the hours like a kid before Christmas.
Cooked the whole wedding breakfast for sixty on my own. Every plate went out hot. I know what I'm worth now.
Dani's wedding was pure joy. Danced till two, lost a shoe, found it in the pond. Best night of the year.
Dani's hen weekend is in nine days and the plans are getting out of hand. I cannot wait.
